newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Aros reduces P&U trading recommendation to reduce.
newsitem.headline: Aros reduces P&U trading recommendation to reduce.

text.p: Swedish brokerage Aros said on Wednesday it had cut its trading recommendation on U.S./Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn (P&U) to 'reduce' from 'accumulate' after a company visit.
Aros analysts said they had a "renewed sense of disappointment" after visiting the company in Stockholm on Tuesday this week.

"We believe that the underlying sales and earnings trends seen in quarter one 1997 remain, as P&U continues to feel pressure from declining sales in several products areas," Aros said in a stock report.
It said this would be made worse by generic competition and heavy investments in the launch phases of recently and soon-to-be launched drugs.

"Although the sales and earnings picture remains too uncertain at the present time to predict with surety, we believe that the company will show flat to declining sales and earnings in each of the next three quarters," Aros said.
It lowered its EPS estimate for 1997 by 12 cents to $1.71 compared to consensus of $1.90. Aros forecast second quarter 1997 EPS of $0.39 against consensus of $0.50.
For 1998 it saw EPS at $2.00 and for 1999 at $2.30.
Aros said it saw P&U share trading in the $30 range until uncertainties over sales and earnings were made clear.
"In addition, given the potential newsflow in the coming quarter, we believe there remains a significant investment risk in the share in the near-term," Aros said.
"However over the longer term and after this period of difficulty we remain confident that P&U will eventually right itself."
P&U, which has issued three profit warnings over the past 12 months, was trading 9.5 crowns lower at 255.5 crowns on the Stockholm bourse at 1315 GMT.
